$comment: PCI DSS v4.0.1 → ISO/IEC 27001:2022 Annex A control mappings. Written against the intent of each requirement (original paraphrases — PCI SSC text is copyrighted). PCI DSS requirements are prescriptive and CDE-scoped while Annex A controls are outcome-level and org-wide, so most relationships are 'partial': the PCI control satisfies the Annex A intent inside the CDE but not necessarily enterprise-wide.
source: PCI DSS v4.0.1 requirement-intent cross-walk to ISO/IEC 27001:2022 Annex A

mappings.rationale: NSC ruleset configuration standards implement network security management.
Current network diagrams document the asset landscape the inventory control expects.
Semi-annual ruleset reviews keep network controls aligned with need.
Restricting traffic into the CDE is network segregation.
Mediating trusted/untrusted boundaries is core network security control.
Host-level controls on dual-connected devices protect user endpoints.
Both require established, maintained configuration/hardening standards.
Eliminating vendor defaults is a specific configuration-management outcome.
Disabling unnecessary services is minimal-footprint configuration management.
Encrypting non-console administrative sessions applies cryptography to management traffic.
Deleting account data at end of retention is information deletion.
Retention schedules for account data support records-management requirements.
PAN display masking is data masking applied to account data.
Rendering stored PAN unreadable via hashing/encryption/tokenization applies cryptographic protection.
Protecting data-encrypting keys is the key-management half of the cryptography control.
Key lifecycle (generation, distribution, rotation, retirement) is cryptographic key management.
Strong transport cryptography for PAN is cryptography-in-transit.
Protecting PAN over public networks secures information transfer.
Both require anti-malware protection across in-scope systems.
Periodic/real-time scanning is the operational half of malware protection.
Anti-phishing mechanisms complement awareness training against social engineering.
Both require a secure development lifecycle for software.
Preventing injection and similar attack classes is secure-coding practice.
Both require identifying and risk-ranking technical vulnerabilities from industry sources.
Software/component inventories (SBOM) extend the asset inventory to code dependencies.
Time-bound patching operationalises vulnerability management.
A WAF in blocking mode is an application-security requirement for public-facing apps.
Both require formal change management for production systems.
A need-to-know access model with default deny is access-control policy.
Least-privilege assignment including privileged users overlaps privileged-access management.
Semi-annual account/privilege reviews are the review half of access-rights management.
Unique IDs per user are identity-management fundamentals.
Immediate revocation for terminated users is access-rights removal.
Lockout after failed attempts is a secure-authentication mechanism.
Minimum password strength is authentication-information management.
MFA into the CDE is a strong-authentication requirement; PCI mandates it universally for CDE access.
Banning hard-coded credentials in code/scripts is a secure-coding rule.
Facility entry controls around CDE systems establish physical security perimeters.
Visitor authorization, escort and badging are physical-entry controls.
Securing media holding cardholder data (incl. offsite backups) is storage-media control.
Destroying media when no longer needed matches secure disposal/re-use of equipment.
Both require audit logs of user, admin and system-level events.
Tamper-protection and central backup of logs is part of the logging control.
Daily automated log review is monitoring for anomalous activity.
The 12-month log-retention floor supports records protection; the exact period is PCI-specific.
Both require synchronized clocks from protected time sources.
Detecting failures of security-control systems is a monitoring outcome.
Quarterly internal vulnerability scanning operationalises technical vulnerability management.
Quarterly external ASV scanning extends vulnerability management to the perimeter.
Penetration testing validates vulnerability management beyond scanning; ISO has no explicit pentest control.
Segmentation testing verifies the effectiveness of network segregation.
IDS/IPS at CDE boundaries is technical monitoring for intrusions.
File-integrity change detection monitors for unauthorized modification.
Both require an approved, published and communicated information security policy.
The annual policy review matches planned-interval policy review.
Annual scope confirmation depends on a complete inventory of information and assets.
Both require a formal security awareness programme.
On-hire and annual training with acknowledgement delivers the awareness programme.
Both require pre-hire screening proportionate to role and law.
The TPSP register manages security in supplier relationships.
Written responsibility acknowledgements put security into supplier agreements.
Annual monitoring of TPSP compliance status is supplier-service review.
Both require a maintained incident-response plan with roles and communication paths.
Annual IR plan testing and lessons-learned updates keep incident preparation current.
